aggregation: For each batch, pooled median of four families times three unfenced repetitions (12 samples) per main timer. Ratios are ratios of these medians. Fenced substage medians use four independent family profiles and do not sum to the whole-step median.

interpretation: B128 GPU is slower than native ten-worker control; B256 is near parity in this run, and B512 is faster.
No allocator or physical-memory guard failed at B128/B256/B512. The 3 GB fixed MPS allocator reservation was unchanged. B512 remained below the 7 GB conservative stop threshold inside its 8 GB guard.
Workloads preserve all lanes, candidate choices, state/history fields and exact RNG. No further size was attempted after the requested sequential128/256/512 follow-up.
limits: Only supported recruitment chance transitions on a constructed controlled-minor fixture population.
Repeated identical immutable source per lane; certified-source hits do not establish chronological-game hit rate.
CPU ten-worker pool is an explicit diagnostic; production CPU search is not automatically parallelized by this measurement.
Larger-batch crossover does not establish full-game, search, training speed or useful learned play.
Intrusive stage fences and retained buffers are separate from unfenced whole-step timing.
